# Home-style chicken noodle soup

A cup of canned chicken noodle soup has about 830 mg sodium. Made at home with low-sodium broth, herbs and lemon, a big bowl (about 1½ cups) has about 130 mg. **Soup counts as fluid:** on a fluid limit, a bowl uses about 350 mL of your allowance, so plan for it or have a smaller bowl.

**Serves 4** · 35 minutes · Lower potassium · Lower phosphorus · Freezes well

!!! abstract "Carbohydrate per serving"
    **22 g carbohydrate** (about 1½ carb choices of 15 g). That is not much for a meal. For a lunch of about 55 g, add 1 slice of white bread (14 g) and ½ cup of canned pineapple in juice (20 g), or more pasta in the soup.

Checked by `scripts/build_handbook.py`: sodium at most 600 mg per serving; "lower potassium" means at most 600 mg and "lower phosphorus" at most 300 mg per serving. See [how recipes are checked](index.md#how-the-recipes-are-checked).

Ingredients that are not in the app's food list (herbs, spices and a few others) add about 12 mg potassium per serving; they are counted above.

## Ingredients

| Ingredient | Amount | Grams |
|---|---|---|
| Olive oil | 1 tbsp olive oil | 14 g |
| Onion, raw | ½ cup chopped onion | 80 g |
| Celery, raw | 1 stalk celery, sliced | 40 g |
| Carrot, raw | 1 medium carrot, sliced thin | 61 g |
| Garlic, raw | 2 cloves garlic, chopped | 6.0 g |
| Chicken broth, low sodium, canned | 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth (check the label for potassium chloride) | 960 g |
| Water, tap | 2 cups water | 474 g |
| Thyme, dried | ½ tsp dried thyme | 0.5 g |
| Black pepper, ground | ¼ tsp black pepper | 0.6 g |
| Chicken breast, roasted, skinless | 6 oz cooked chicken breast, diced (about 1½ cups) | 170 g |
| Pasta, cooked | 1½ cups cooked small pasta shapes or broken spaghetti, cooked without salt | 186 g |
| Parsley, fresh | 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley | 7.6 g |
| Lemon juice, fresh | 1 tbsp lemon juice | 15 g |

## Steps

1. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery and carrot for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 more minute.
2. Add the broth, water, thyme and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the carrot is tender.
3. Add the chicken and cooked pasta and heat until steaming, about 5 minutes.
4. Turn off the heat and stir in the parsley and lemon juice. Taste before adding anything: lemon and pepper usually do the job of salt.

## Why it works for kidneys

- The potassium from the carrot and celery stays in the broth, so it counts even though they are boiled. One carrot for 4 bowls keeps it low.
- Some low-sodium broths use potassium chloride instead of salt. Read the ingredient list and pick one without it.
- Cook the pasta separately and add it at the end so it does not soak up the broth.

## Make it fit you

- **On a fluid limit:** serve 1 cup of soup with extra chicken and pasta in the bowl, so you get the same food with less liquid.
- **Freeze:** freeze the soup without the pasta for up to 3 months; add freshly cooked pasta when you reheat it.
- **Rice instead of pasta:** ¾ cup cooked white rice for the pot.
